sections.heading: What is Union Find?
sections.content: Union Find (also called Disjoint Set Union, or DSU) tracks a collection of items split into groups that never overlap. It supports two operations: find(x) tells you which group x belongs to (by returning the group's representative, or root), and union(a, b) merges the groups of a and b. With two optimizations, path compression and union by size or rank, both operations run in nearly constant time, O(α(n)), where α is the inverse Ackermann function and is below 5 for any realistic input.

sections.heading: When to Use It
items: Connectivity queries: are two nodes in the same group?
Count connected components while edges are added over time (dynamic connectivity)
Detect a cycle in an undirected graph (an edge whose endpoints are already connected)
Merge groups by shared properties (accounts with a common email, equal variables)
Kruskal's algorithm for minimum spanning trees
Grid problems where land cells are added one by one
Group indices that can be swapped, then sort within each group
Keywords: connected, group, merge, same set, redundant connection, components, equivalence, union

sections.heading: The Intuition
sections.content: Imagine every person at a party starts as their own group, each with themselves as the leader. When two people become friends, their groups merge: one leader now reports to the other. To check whether two people are in the same group, follow the 'leader' chain from each person to the top and compare the two top leaders. Path compression flattens the chain after you walk it, and union by size always attaches the smaller group under the larger one, so chains stay very short.

Mapping Problems to Indices
items: Nodes labeled 0 to n - 1: use the label directly
Nodes labeled 1 to n: create UnionFind(n + 1) and ignore index 0
Grid cell (r, c): use id = r * cols + c
Letters 'a' to 'z': use c - 'a' with UnionFind(26)
Strings, emails or large sparse numbers: map to indices with a HashMap, or use MapUnionFind
Rows and columns as separate nodes: offset the column ids so they do not collide with row ids

sections.heading: Common Mistakes
items: Linking the nodes themselves instead of their roots, which breaks the group structure
Skipping path compression or union by size, which can degrade operations to O(n)
Using an array of size n for 1-indexed nodes (use n + 1)
Forgetting to decrement the component count only when a union actually merges two groups
Using Union Find on a directed graph, where edge direction matters
Reading parent[x] instead of find(x) when asking for the group, since parent is not always the root
Letting row and column ids collide when modeling both in one structure (add an offset)
Recursive find on a very long chain (use the iterative version when n is huge and compression has not run yet)

sections.heading: Key Takeaways
items: Union Find maintains disjoint groups with find (which group?) and union (merge groups)
Path compression plus union by size gives near-constant O(α(n)) operations
A union that returns false means the two items were already connected, which detects cycles
Track the number of components by decreasing it on every successful merge
Map grid cells, letters and strings to integer ids so one array-based structure works
Choose Union Find when connections arrive over time or when you only need group membership, and DFS or BFS when you need paths
